fact: The first World Cup had just 13 teams, and most European sides skipped the three-week boat trip to South America.
Italy won at home in the first World Cup to need qualifying matches. The holders, Uruguay, refused to take part.
Italy became the first team to defend the World Cup. The next tournament wasn't played until 1950 because of the Second World War.
Uruguay stunned around 200,000 fans at the Maracanã by beating Brazil in the deciding game. Brazilians still call it the 'Maracanazo'.
West Germany came from 2–0 down to beat Hungary's 'Mighty Magyars', who had been unbeaten for four years. Germans call it the 'Miracle of Bern'.
A 17-year-old Pelé scored twice in the final as Brazil won their first World Cup.
Brazil retained the trophy even though Pelé was injured early in the tournament. Garrincha took over as their star.
Geoff Hurst scored the only hat-trick in a World Cup final until Kylian Mbappé in 2022. Before the tournament the trophy was stolen, and a dog called Pickles found it.
The first World Cup shown in colour on television. Brazil's third title let them keep the original Jules Rimet trophy.
The Netherlands scored from a penalty before West Germany had touched the ball, but the hosts came back to win in Munich.
Mario Kempes scored twice in the final and was the tournament's top scorer as Argentina won their first World Cup.
Paolo Rossi, who had only just returned from a ban, scored six goals to win the Golden Boot as Italy won their third title.
Diego Maradona dominated the tournament, including both of his famous goals against England in the quarter-final.
Andreas Brehme's late penalty won the final. Franz Beckenbauer became the second man to win the World Cup as both player and coach.
The first World Cup final decided on penalties. Roberto Baggio, Italy's star, missed the last one.
Zinedine Zidane headed two goals as the hosts won their first World Cup.
Ronaldo scored both goals in the final and eight in the tournament, as Brazil won a record fifth title.
Zinedine Zidane was sent off in extra time of his last ever match, for headbutting Marco Materazzi.
Andrés Iniesta scored late in extra time to give Spain their first World Cup, in the first tournament held in Africa.
Mario Götze's extra-time volley won the final, days after Germany beat the hosts Brazil 7–1 in the semi-final.
France won their second title with a young team including 19-year-old Kylian Mbappé. VAR was used at a World Cup for the first time.
Often called the greatest final ever: Messi scored twice and Mbappé scored a hat-trick before Argentina won on penalties.
